title: Takht Patna Sahib
hook: at Patna, where the Tenth Guru was born

segments.voice: Yesterday, Takht Damdama Sahib, at Talwandi Sabo, where the Granth was completed. Your line was the guru's rest. Where did you find a still place, even for a minute? Day one thousand two hundred eighty-two.

A birth certificate holds a town, a date and two names. It doesn't hold the river outside the window, or the sound of the street, or who was carrying the baby when the visitors came. Sikhs remember the Tenth Guru's birth through a place. Far to the east of Punjab, in the city of Patna, near the wide Ganges, there is a gurdwara built where tradition says Guru Gobind Singh was born. It is one of the Takhts, the seats of authority we have been visiting these last days. The others we've met sit in Punjab. This one sits a long way from there, because the Guru's life began far from where most of his story would be told.
screen: `A CERTIFICATE HOLDS A TOWN.` → `PATNA, BY THE GANGES.` → `A TAKHT FAR FROM PUNJAB.`

segments.voice: Start with why the family was there at all. Tradition says the Ninth Guru, Guru Tegh Bahadur, was traveling in the east, and his family stayed in Patna while he went on. So the boy who would become the Tenth Guru was born while his father was away on the road. His childhood name, tradition says, was Gobind Rai. Then come the stories people tell about those early years. A boy by the river, playing at soldiers with other children, organizing games of mock battle. A boy who drew the love of the neighbors. Sikhs tell of a woman in the town who had no child of her own and who longed to hold him, and of the food and care she gave him. These are told as stories of the childhood, kept by the community, and they are told warmly. Then the turn. The family left Patna and went west to Punjab, and the Guru's life after that moves through Anandpur, battle, loss and the founding of the Khalsa. Patna stayed behind as the place of the beginning. That's what makes this Takht different from the others. Akal Takht faces the Harmandir. Keshgarh marks where the Khalsa was born. Damdama marks where the Granth was completed. Patna marks something smaller and more ordinary: a birth, and a little boy's first years. Sikhs today travel there to stand where he was a child. The full name of the place calls it Takht Sri Harimandir Ji, Patna Sahib, and visitors are shown things kept in memory of the Guru's childhood. A seat of authority, built on a nursery. Where he was born.
screen: `HIS FATHER AWAY ON THE ROAD.` · `A BOY BY THE RIVER.` · `THE FAMILY GOES WEST.` · `A SEAT BUILT ON A CHILDHOOD.` · then, large: `WHERE HE WAS BORN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: picture a child by the Ganges. Settle, and breathe. See a wide, slow river and a bank of mud and steps. See a small boy there, barefoot, with other children around him, loud and busy with some game. Nobody watching him knows yet what his life will hold. Let him just be a child. If you like, let your mind drift to a place where you were small, and the first river or street or yard you remember. Stay with the boy, and with the river, until the bell. The bell holds the time.
Takht Patna Sahib. The seat of authority in Patna, in the east, built where tradition says Guru Gobind Singh was born and spent his first years. Today's word.
Your line: where he was born. Today, ask someone you love where they were born, and what they remember of it. Listen to the small details. Day one thousand two hundred eighty-two.

howItsDone: Sikhs visit Takht Patna Sahib to honor the Tenth Guru's birthplace, and the gurdwara keeps items remembered from his childhood for pilgrims to see.
